precepts.point: Right? The Lord showed him something that nobody could see. Open his eyes, and he could see what's behind him. In the spiritual realm, there's angels all around us. The Lord said, where two or three gather, I'm in the midst of you. We don't see that. But the Lord will open up his spirit to make it evident. And I have some images on that too, if you look in there, angels in the heavens, that will reveal those things. But you have to move from milk to meat to tap into that. Again, if you still caught up in your old sins, you ain't going to be able to see these things. You're not going to be able to have foresight. note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
Elisha prayed, “Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see”, and the young man saw “the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.” The Lord showed him something nobody could see: he opened his eyes, and he could see what was behind him. In the spiritual realm, there are angels all around us.

The Lord said it: “where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.” We don't see that. But the Lord will open up his spirit to make it evident, the way he opened the young man's eyes.

There will come a time when some of us will see things, and God will whisper in our ears, show us, direct our path and reveal things to us. That is one of the spiritual senses being activated, and part of it is having foresight.

But you have to move from milk to meat to tap into that. If you are still caught up in your old sins, you ain't going to be able to see these things. The Lord is in the midst of his people when they gather in his name; it is the ones who have come out of their sins whose eyes he opens to see it.

precepts.text: A host surrounded the city with horses and chariots, and Elisha's servant said, Alas, my master! how shall we do? A whole army came for this one prophet. And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them. Elisha prayed, Lord, open his eyes, that he may see: and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire. Those were angels waiting for the word. You cannot see things spiritually, but understand: the Lord is with us, his angels are with us, and the Lord is fighting with us. There is no way we could do what the Lord sent us to do on this earth, and no way you would see the growth of IUIC and of Israel, if he were not with us. And prepare your mind: it is going to be the same in the future; they came for one prophet, and they will come with agents and lies for those who teach the word of God. Read about COINTELPRO and ask yourself if you think that stopped.
precepts.point: For the battle is not yours, but God's. Why does it say the battle belongs to the Lord? Because the Lord is always there fighting with you.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
“for the battle is not yours, but God’s.” Why does the battle belong to the Lord? Because the Lord is always there fighting with you, even though you cannot see him. Even when you are doing evil, the angels are right there watching and writing down everything you do; the eyes of the Lord are open on all of us. For those who do not believe the Lord is with them and fighting with them, for those with weak faith, look at Elisha.

“And when the servant of the man of God was risen early, and gone forth, behold, an host compassed the city both with horses and chariots. And his servant said unto him, Alas, my master! how shall we do?” A whole army surrounded the city, and they came for this one prophet, this one brother.

“And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.” As men of God you have to realize the Lord is always with you, and those with you are stronger than those with the enemy. “And Elisha prayed, and said, Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the Lord opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.” Chariots of fire: angels, just waiting for the word. A man’s army surrounded Elisha, and the Lord’s army surrounded that army, waiting to set it off.

You cannot see things spiritually, but understand: the Lord is with us, his angels are with us, and the Lord is fighting with us. There is no way we could do what the Lord sent us to do on this earth, and no way you would see the growth of IUIC and of Israel, if he were not with us. And it will be the same in the future: they came for one prophet, and federal agents will surround the houses of some of you who teach the word of God. That is the mind you have to have. So be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of the great multitude.

precepts.text: In the siege of Samaria an ass's head sold for fourscore pieces of silver, and a woman said, Give thy son, that we may eat him to day; so we boiled my son, and did eat him.
precepts.point: Eating the flesh of sons and daughters goes into 70 AD, and it also happened in the days of the kings when the city was besieged and there was such famine that a woman's son was boiled and eaten.

note.label: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses

precepts.why:
The Most High said He would walk contrary in fury and would be the one doing it: He would use the enemies, but it would be Him behind it. That is heavy. And eating the flesh of sons and daughters happened in the days of the kings, when the city was besieged and there was such famine that a woman’s son was boiled and eaten.

In the days of the kings “there was a great famine in Samaria: and, behold, they besieged it, until an ass’s head was sold for fourscore pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a cab of dove’s dung for five pieces of silver.” As the king of Israel was passing by upon the wall a woman cried to him for help, and when he asked what ailed her, she answered: “This woman said unto me, Give thy son, that we may eat him to day, and we will eat my son to morrow. So we boiled my son, and did eat him: and I said unto her on the next day, Give thy son, that we may eat him: and she hath hid her son.”

The king could only say, “If the Lord do not help thee, whence shall I help thee?” That is the curse of Leviticus 26 carried out on Israel to the letter.

precepts.text: The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.
precepts.point: Elisha prays that the Lord open the young man's eyes, and the Lord opens them so he sees the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha. When Israel goes out to war, there is more with them than with their enemies, for the angels of the Lord are with them.

note.label: 2 Kings 6: The Floating Axe Head and the Blinded Host

precepts.why:
“The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.” That is what the young man saw when his eyes were opened.

The king of Syria sent “horses, and chariots, and a great host” by night to Dothan to fetch Elisha, and they compassed the city about. The servant rose early, saw the host, and cried, “Alas, my master! how shall we do?” Elisha answered, “Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.” He prayed, “Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see”, and “behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.”

Round about the man of God, just as the psalm says the angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him. When Israel goes out to war, there is more with them than with their enemies, for the angels of the Lord are with them.

precepts.text: In the siege and straitness of the enemy, a disobedient Israel shall eat the fruit of their own body, the flesh of their sons and daughters, which is the curse fulfilled in this famine.
precepts.point: The woman tells how another woman said, give thy son that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow, so they boiled and ate her son, but the next day the other woman hid her son. When the king hears this, he rends his clothes, and the people see he has sackcloth upon his flesh, and he swears that the head of Elisha shall not stand on him this day.

note.label: 2 Kings 6: The Floating Axe Head and the Blinded Host

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and of thy daughters, which the Lord thy God hath given thee, in the siege, and in the straitness, wherewith thine enemies shall distress thee:” That is the curse on a disobedient Israel, and in Samaria it came to pass.

Ben-hadad king of Syria besieged Samaria, and the famine was so great that “an ass’s head was sold for fourscore pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a cab of dove’s dung for five pieces of silver.” A woman cried to the king on the wall and told him, “This woman said unto me, Give thy son, that we may eat him to day, and we will eat my son to morrow. So we boiled my son, and did eat him”. The next day the other woman hid her son.

The siege, the straitness, the enemy distressing them, and mothers eating the flesh of their sons: the curse fulfilled. The king had no help to give, “If the Lord do not help thee, whence shall I help thee?” He rent his clothes, the people saw “he had sackcloth within upon his flesh”, and he swore that the head of Elisha would not stand on him that day.

precepts.text: Elisha's servant sees the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire, for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.
precepts.point: The Most High smites the Ethiopians before Asa; they flee and are destroyed, and Judah carries away very much spoil. Faith in the Most High, not the numbers of the enemy, wins the battle.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 14: Asa Seeks the Most High and Finds Rest

precepts.why:
An host compassed the city with horses and chariots, and Elisha's servant cried, “Alas, my master! how shall we do? And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.” Elisha prayed, “And the Lord opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.” And the Lord smote the enemy with blindness “according to the word of Elisha.”

Asa faced the same: Zerah the Ethiopian, a Cushite, came out “with an host of a thousand thousand, and three hundred chariots.” And Asa cried, “Lord, it is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power.”

“So the Lord smote the Ethiopians before Asa, and before Judah; and the Ethiopians fled.” They were destroyed “before the Lord, and before his host”, and Judah carried away very much spoil. Faith in the Most High, not the numbers of the enemy, wins the battle.

points: As they fell wood by Jordan, one man's axe head falls into the water, and he cries out to Elisha, alas master, for it was borrowed. The axe was not his own.

points: Elisha asks where it fell, the man shows him the place, and Elisha cuts down a stick and casts it in, and the iron swims. Though iron sinks by nature, the Lord makes it float, and Elisha tells the man to take it up, and he reaches out his hand and takes it.

note.label: 2 Kings 6: The Floating Axe Head and the Blinded Host

points: The king of Syria wars against Israel and takes counsel with his servants, choosing where to set his camp. But the man of God sends to the king of Israel warning him to beware of passing a certain place, because the Syrians have come down there.

note.label: 2 Kings 6: The Floating Axe Head and the Blinded Host

points: The king of Israel sends to the place Elisha warned him of and saves himself, not once nor twice, so the heart of the king of Syria is sore troubled. He calls his servants and asks which of them is for the king of Israel.

note.label: 2 Kings 6: The Floating Axe Head and the Blinded Host

points: One servant answers that none of them is, but Elisha the prophet in Israel tells the king of Israel the very words the king of Syria speaks in his bedchamber.

note.label: 2 Kings 6: The Floating Axe Head and the Blinded Host

note.label: 2 Kings 6: The Floating Axe Head and the Blinded Host

points: While Elisha yet talks with them, the messenger comes down and says, behold, this evil is of the Lord; what should I wait for the Lord any longer. The king and his messenger blame the Lord for the evil and lose patience for his deliverance.
